fields.statement: QA at 1f3f071f with the built binary (go build ./cmd/rhiza) in a scratch git repo, hermetic HOME, fake claude (dumps .claude.json at start) and fake rex: rhiza session start --permission-mode manual, then session run --dry-run left ~/.claude.json (numStartups, theme, projects./other.allowedTools) unchanged; the real session run set hasTrustDialogAccepted=true for the main checkout root (repo) and the session worktree (repo.qa-trust) before the agent started (the fake claude saw both), kept numStartups, theme and /other.allowedTools and the file mode 0640, left no temp file. With CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to an empty dir, session run created $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json (0600) with both paths trusted and left HOME's file byte-identical. go test -run 'Trust|CommandWritesNoFile' for internal/api and claudecode passes (resume re-trust and Command writing no file are covered there). The owner's real ~/.claude.json uses the same hasTrustDialogAccepted key under projects.

QA at 1f3f071f with the built binary, hermetic HOME and fake claude: with ~/.claude.json set to '{nope', rhiza session run still started the agent (fake claude ran in the worktree, exit 0) and printed 'Warning: trust the session's folders in <HOME>/.claude.json: read the Claude Code config: invalid character ...'; the file stayed byte-for-byte '{nope' and no .claude.json.rhiza-* temp file was left in HOME.
